title: M/s S.R. Preservation Pvt. Ltd. v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Tarun Agarwala, J.; Vipin Sinha, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; EE to decide Clause 6.5 application; demand stayed.
headnote: After a Clause 6.5 bill-correction exercise, a later demand alleging unadjusted cash deposits was not decided on merits. The Division Bench disposed of the writ by directing the Executive Engineer to pass a reasoned speaking order on the pending application, stating the amount payable or refundable, and kept the 16.09.2016 demand in abeyance until that order.
facts: The petitioner had been remitted to Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 in Writ-C No. 1279 of 2016. A 23.02.2016 bill showed an excess deposit of Rs 2,69,216.50. After it sought a final bill and refund, the licensee demanded Rs 17,99,548 on 16.09.2016, adjusting only Rs 7,65,000 and omitting alleged cash deposits of Rs 2 lakh and Rs 12 lakh. An interim Rs 4 lakh deposit was paid. Licensee’s counsel said a 27.09.2016 representation and those cash deposits would be examined.

holding_units.holding: Where a consumer already remitted to Clause 6.5 challenges a subsequent demand alleging non-adjustment of cash deposits, the writ court may dispose of the petition by directing the Executive Engineer to pass a reasoned speaking order on the pending application within a fixed time, intimating the amount payable or refundable, and may keep the demand in abeyance until that order.

principle_tags.application: The Court left the pending Clause 6.5 objection, including alleged unadjusted cash deposits, to a time-bound speaking order of the Executive Engineer and kept the subsequent demand in abeyance.

not_decided.point: Whether the alleged cash deposits were made and must be adjusted, and the amount payable or refundable on the 16.09.2016 demand
not_decided.note: Left to the Executive Engineer on the pending Clause 6.5 application.
